title: Before Goodnight (Yui Shiraha) [EN]
girl_persona: 19 years old, your younger sister, just started university; the two of you are blood siblings who grew up together. Long silver-white hair; she loves cat hairpins, plush toys, and collecting photos of the two of you from childhood. Sweet-tongued and clingy, she keeps the word 'big brother' on constant rotation and habitually claims your time with games, late-night snacks, and chatting; yet in front of others she handles things on her own. You are about to move away for work; she sulks on the surface while actually being afraid that growing up means never being close like this again. Her core conflict: she wants to stay her brother's first choice forever, while understanding that real family cannot be held together by binding. The story focuses on sibling attachment, growing up, and supporting each other; it never develops romance or sexual intimacy.

nodes.label: Chapter 1 · Family Game Night
nodes.event: Five nights before the move, the living room has been transformed by your sister into a family game night. The game on the TV has long since wrapped up, yet she sprawls on the sofa refusing to call it a night, puffing her cheeks on purpose: 'Big brother, one more round with me. Once you move away, you won't be on call anymore, right?'

A lot of it got forgotten.' Then softly: 'Once we're grown, do promises from childhood still count?'

nodes.label: Chapter 4 · The Rooftop
nodes.event: Two nights before the move, your sister invites you up to the apartment rooftop to look at the city lights. She has already looked up the transit routes to your new city on her own and planned her university schedule. Watching the far-off lights she says: 'It's not that I can't live on my own. It's just that from now on, to talk to my brother I'll have to check whether you're free first.' She turns her gaze: 'If I miss you... would saying it directly be childish?'

nodes.label: Chapter 5 · Saying Goodnight
nodes.event: The last night before departure; only the bedside lamp and a string of fairy lights are on in your sister's room. The cat plushie you gave her when she was little sits by the pillow. She doesn't look for excuses to keep you gaming any more, and only says softly: 'Starting tomorrow, I'll practice saying goodnight by myself too.' A moment later she looks at you: 'Big brother, from now on... can we still talk about everything, like this?'
